digest.component_or_area: rebar._store git operations under high local concurrency
propositions: Local git call sites across rebar._commands and rebar.metrics lack bounded contention policy and retries, causing errors to surface to agents instead of being absorbed when peer processes briefly hold .git/index.lock or ref locks under high concurrent local use.

Per-store advisory flock serialization plus jittered bounded retry on git's own lock signatures (index.lock, ref locks) allows transient conflicts to self-heal silently while only permanently stuck locks surface one actionable error naming the contended lock file and holder guidance.

Uncontended store git operations must add zero latency: the advisory lock's fast path is non-blocking flock, and retry sleeps only occur on actual contention, preserving existing performance on the happy path.

Local-only git call sites (run_git_write, fsck read paths, metrics walks) must be bounded by watchdog timeouts justified against local latency (120s for plumbing, 300s for slow walks like blame/log), not copied from network values, and distinguish wedged filesystem from slow work.

Stale-lock reclamation and contention handling must never escalate or block forever; git-level retry with jittered backoff (uniform 0.75–1.25x multiplier on exponential schedule, capped per-sleep, ~20s total budget) combined with per-store advisory lock prevents thundering herd while remaining safe under containerization and NFS.

The store's blocking policy under local contention is explicitly bounded jittered retry plus advisory serialization: silent transient recovery, one actionable error only on stuck lock, no escalation to the agent, consistent with push-retry precedent and operator-ratified decision 2026-08-04.
